This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #32361: TUI hangs on black screen (OpenTUI) — similar blank screen symptom, different trigger (startup vs. during agent work), same underlying renderer
- #33887: TUI shows black screen regression on WSL — blank screen with no input possible
- #35494: TUI freezes with blank screen (Debian) — render loop fires but produces zero output, similar stall behavior

If your issue is specifically triggered *during agent work* (not at startup), it may be a distinct race condition as you've described. But linking these for cross-reference may help track down a shared root cause.

Thanks for the cross-references. I checked all three:

- **#32361** (black at boot, Wayland) and **#33887** (WSL regression at v1.17.10): These are **startup** hangs — the terminal-capability DCS query phase deadlocks before any render loop runs. Different root cause from the render-loop-stall described here.

- **#35494** (Debian 13, renders zero output): Most likely related — the reporter notes "Render loop timer fires every 1s but produces zero output." This could share the same `requestRender()` → `loop()` → `finally` race documented here, triggered during the initial render burst at startup rather than during agent work. The workaround of switching terminal tabs (SIGWINCH → `handleResize` → `requestRender()`) might also work for that case.

All four issues trace back to the same fragile render-loop scheduling in `@opentui/core` `CliRenderer` — the gap between flag checks and the `finally` block where re-render requests are silently dropped.

Thanks for the great project! I accidentally opened two PRs for the same DaoXE provider docs — closing this one in favor of #37798, which is the one I'll keep updated per any feedback. Sorry for the noise, and thanks for your time. 🙏

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #30197: Desktop: background dependency install failed - @opencode-ai/plugin@local version not found
- #30908: Server: background dependency install fails every session with @opencode-ai/plugin@local not found (includes detailed root cause analysis)
- #37024: [Bug] Startup Warning: NpmInstallFailedError for @opencode-ai/plugin@local
- #31708: Desktop app hangs on Windows 11 - @opencode-ai/plugin@local npm install failed

All of these report the same underlying issue: `OPENCODE_VERSION` not being substituted at build time, causing the app to use `@local` as the npm version specifier, which does not exist on the registry.

If you believe this was flagged incorrectly, please let a maintainer know.

UPDATE
- I looked into the root cause: for `pull_request_review_comment` events, the action still calls the issue-comments API (`rest.issues.createComment`), so the reply lands on the PR timeline instead of inside the review thread
- I have opened PR #37574 to fix this by adding an `if` block that calls `rest.pulls.createReplyForReviewComment` for review-comment triggers
- I made a demo repo to reproduce this issue: https://github.com/chAwater/oc-github-test/pulls

Hey! Your PR title `perf(opencode): coalesce code mode progress updates` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes

Rebased onto the current `dev` branch, resolved the project-store changes, regenerated the SDK, and reran the focused tests, full typechecks, all three 210-route HTTP API exerciser modes, production Web build, standalone binary build, and a fresh-browser cross-origin smoke test. Thanks for working on this. I think adding --ignore-cr-at-eol is a workaround rather than addressing the root cause.

The Git service currently overrides repository/user configuration with:
```text
-c core.autocrlf=false
-c core.symlinks=true
```
On Windows, this can conflict with a checkout using core.autocrlf=true and core.symlinks=false. The former causes CRLF-only false positives, while the latter causes symlink placeholders such as packages/docs/openapi.json and various PNG/ICO/SVG/manifest files to appear as type changes or deletions. These files are stored as mode 120000 in Git.

--ignore-cr-at-eol also only affects git diff; git status can remain inconsistent, and legitimate CR changes may be hidden.

A more complete fix would be to stop overriding these two settings and let Git respect the repository/user configuration:
```diff
 const cfg = [
   "--no-optional-locks",
-  "-c",
-  "core.autocrlf=false",
   "-c",
   "core.fsmonitor=false",
   "-c",
   "core.longpaths=true",
-  "-c",
-  "core.symlinks=true",
   "-c",
   "core.quotepath=false",
 ] as const
```
It would also be useful to add regression tests for a CRLF checkout with core.autocrlf=true and a symlink placeholder checkout with core.symlinks=false. This should fix both issues without changing the intended diff semantics.

Same symptom as OP. Some extra details that might help narrow the fix:

Environment
- Windows 11, Chrome/Edge (latest)
- opencode web (default port 4096, loopback only)
- opencode version: 1.18.3 (running on C:\Users\Solac)
- Loaded plugin: oh-my-openagent (irrelevant — issue reproduces without per OP)
- Browser localStorage cleared / fresh profile
- No project added to the opened-project list

Diagnostics beyond OP's report

1. POST /api/session works fine from fetch() in DevTools console — backend is healthy.
2. The titlebar button (button[aria-label="新建会话"]) exists, disabled=false, correct position.
3. Programmatic button.click() does NOT navigate and does NOT call any fetch — i.e. the click handler is not bound / is a no-op. This rules out "calls API but UI doesn't update".
4. Console is silent (zero errors, zero warnings during the click).
5. Workaround that works: bind a manual listener to keydown and fetch('/api/session', {method:'POST', headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body:'{}'}) then location.href = '/' + data.data.id. The frontend API + render path is fine; only the titlebar button is broken.

Hypothesis: the titlebar New Session action returns early because no project is selected, and the fallback path to sdk.directory (which OP mentions in the issue body) isn't wired up — so the click handler runs but produces no side effect.

A live `0.0.0-next-15839` snapshot shows this is an active-runtime amplification problem, not only a cold-start or historical-database problem. Across the managed server and connected OpenCode clients, the sample accounted for about 13 GiB RSS and 457% CPU while system CPU was fully occupied. The managed health endpoint still returned healthy, but took 1.78 seconds. No process was restarted or terminated for the measurement.

The newest 10,000 durable events covered about 22 minutes and 23 MiB. Tool success/progress dominated. The largest recent success was 2.43 MiB and came from `webfetch`; its `structured.output` alone was 2.22 MiB. In the 200 largest recent tool events, `webfetch` accounted for 4.55 MiB, with 3.57 MiB in `structured` and another 0.97 MiB in `content`. `read` and `grep` showed the same duplication pattern. `ToolOutputStore.bound` bounds model-facing `content` but preserves the full `structured` value, so large structured output bypasses the practical event budget.

With many TUIs open, the process-global event feed turns this into N-way JSON decode and store projection. This reinforces the landing order: scope delivery by client interest first, then enforce a complete encoded-event budget and store one full blob/reference rather than retaining the same body in both `structured` and `content`. The blob path must remain replay/export aware.
